q: What is the purpose of adjusting entries?
r: To update accounts so revenue and expenses are in the right period
They bring balances up to date before statements are prepared.
w: To erase mistakes from the journal
Errors are fixed with correcting entries.
To increase the balance in the cash account
Adjusting entries are not meant to raise cash.
To close the revenue accounts to zero
That is done by closing entries.

q: Which of these is an adjusting entry item?
r: Depreciation of equipment
It spreads an asset's cost over its useful life.
w: Purchasing a new truck for cash
This is recorded when it happens.

q: What is a prepaid expense?
r: A cost paid in advance that benefits future periods
Prepaid insurance is a common example.
w: A bill that has been received but not paid
That is an accrued expense or payable.
Income received before it is earned
A cost that is never paid

q: What is unearned revenue?
r: Cash received before the service is performed
It is a liability until the work is done.
w: Revenue earned but not yet collected
Profit from the sale of equipment

q: What is accrued revenue?
r: Revenue earned but not yet received or recorded
It is recorded with an adjusting entry.
w: Cash received for work not yet done
Revenue collected in cash on the day of sale

q: What is accrued expense?
r: An expense incurred but not yet paid
Wages owed at period end are one example.
w: An expense paid before it is used
That does not describe an accrual.

q: On December 31, a business owes employees $1,200 in wages that will be paid in January. What adjusting entry is needed?
r: Debit Wages Expense, credit Wages Payable
The expense belongs to December and the amount is owed.
w: This would record paying the wages.
No entry until the wages are paid
Accrual accounting requires recording it in December.

q: A business paid $2,400 for a year of insurance on October 1. What is the insurance expense for the year ended December 31?
r: Three months of a twelve-month policy equals one quarter of the cost.
w: That is six months of coverage.

q: A tutor receives $900 in advance on June 1 for six months of lessons. By June 30, how much has been earned?
r: Each month earns one-sixth of the total.
w: The whole amount is not yet earned.
That is three months of lessons.
One month of lessons was provided.

q: What is the adjusting entry for depreciation?
r: Debit Depreciation Expense, credit Accumulated Depreciation
It records the expense and reduces the asset's book value.

q: Which adjusting entry would create a liability on the balance sheet?
r: Accrued wages expense
Wages owed become Wages Payable.

q: What is the book value of equipment that cost $9,000 and has accumulated depreciation of $3,500?
r: Book value is cost minus accumulated depreciation.
w: This is only the accumulated depreciation.

q: What is the purpose of the worksheet in the accounting cycle?
r: To organize adjustments and balances before statements are prepared
It is an internal tool and not a financial statement.
w: To send to the bank as the final report
The worksheet does not replace the ledger.
To record transactions as they happen
That is the job of the journal.

q: In which order are the financial statements usually prepared?
r: Income statement, statement of owner's equity, balance sheet
Each statement supplies figures needed for the next.
w: Balance sheet, income statement, owner's equity
The balance sheet needs the ending equity figure first.
Owner's equity, balance sheet, income statement
Net income must be found first.
Balance sheet, owner's equity, income statement
This ignores that net income feeds equity.

q: What is the purpose of closing entries?
r: To transfer temporary account balances to owner's equity
They reset revenue and expense accounts for the next period.
w: To adjust asset values to market prices
To correct errors in the journal
Errors are fixed with correcting entries.

q: Which account is used as a temporary clearing account during closing?
r: Income Summary
Revenues and expenses are closed into it before moving to capital.
w: This is a permanent asset account.
This is a permanent liability account.
This is a permanent contra account.

q: What is the first closing entry?
r: Close revenue accounts to Income Summary
Revenue accounts have credit balances, so they are debited to zero.
w: Close the liabilities to expense accounts

q: What does a post-closing trial balance contain?
r: Only permanent accounts
Temporary accounts have been closed to zero.
w: Every account, including the closed ones
This is a temporary account that has been closed.

q: Why is a post-closing trial balance prepared?
r: To confirm debits equal credits after closing
It verifies the ledger is ready for the next period.
w: To record the next period's sales

q: What is a fiscal year?
r: Any 12-month period used for accounting
It may or may not match the calendar year.
w: A period that must start on January 1
Businesses may choose another start date.
A period of exactly six months
A fiscal year is twelve months.
Audits do not define the fiscal year.

q: After adjusting entries, which account would carry a balance on the post-closing trial balance?
r: Accumulated Depreciation
It is a permanent contra-asset account.

q: If an adjusting entry for accrued revenue is omitted, how are the statements affected?
r: Revenue and net income are understated; assets are understated
Earned income was left out of the period.
w: Revenue is overstated and liabilities understated
Omitting an entry cannot overstate revenue.
Expenses are not affected by this omission.
Only the cash balance is wrong
Cash is not affected by an accrual.

q: If the adjusting entry for expired prepaid insurance is omitted, what is the effect?
r: Expenses are understated and assets are overstated
The asset was not reduced and the expense not recorded.
w: Expenses are overstated and assets understated
The effect is the opposite of what happens.

q: A business records $3,000 of rent paid in advance as an expense instead of an asset. What is the effect on the current balance sheet if only part has expired?
r: Assets are understated and equity is understated
The unexpired portion should be an asset.
w: The asset was left out, not overstated.
Expenses were too high, so equity is too low.

q: The adjusted trial balance shows Supplies of $900. A count shows $350 remaining. What adjusting entry is needed?
r: Debit Supplies Expense $550, credit Supplies $550
The supplies used are $900 less $350.
w: Supplies used must be recorded as an expense.

q: Which statement best describes the accounting period concept?
r: Results are reported for specific, equal time periods
This lets users compare performance across periods.
w: A business reports only once, at closing
Periods must always be one year
Periods can be months, quarters or years.

q: What is a reversing entry?
r: An optional entry on the first day of a period that cancels a prior accrual
It simplifies recording the later payment.
w: An entry that cancels a customer's order
That is not an accounting entry.
An entry that closes the revenue accounts
An entry that corrects the trial balance

q: Which entry is used to fix a mistake after it has been posted?
r: A correcting entry
It adjusts the accounts to the proper amounts.
w: This starts a new set of books.

q: A bookkeeper debited Utilities Expense for $180 when the bill was for Telephone Expense. How is it fixed?
r: Debit Telephone Expense, credit Utilities Expense for $180
This moves the amount to the correct account.
w: Debit Utilities Expense, credit Telephone Expense for $180
Erase the original entry from the journal
Debit Cash, credit Utilities Expense for $180
Cash was not involved in the error.

q: What does a bank reconciliation compare?
r: The company's cash records with the bank statement
It explains differences between the two balances.
w: That is not what a reconciliation is.

q: Which item is added to the bank statement balance in a bank reconciliation?
r: Deposits in transit
These were recorded by the company but not yet by the bank.
w: These are subtracted from the bank balance.
These adjust the company's book balance.
These adjust the company's book balance.

q: Which item is subtracted from the bank statement balance in a bank reconciliation?
r: Outstanding checks
The bank has not yet paid these checks.

q: A check you deposited was returned by the bank for insufficient funds. How does the company adjust its books?
r: Decrease cash and increase accounts receivable
The customer still owes the money.
w: Nothing owed by the business changed.

q: What is a petty cash fund used for?
r: Small, routine expenses paid in cash
It avoids writing checks for minor items.
w: Loans are repaid by check or transfer.

q: The petty cash fund holds $200. Receipts total $145 and cash on hand is $52. What is the cash short or over?
r: $3 short
$145 plus $52 equals $197, which is $3 less than $200.
w: The total is below the fund amount.

q: A business discovers that a purchase of equipment for $4,000 on account was never recorded. What effect does the omission have on the accounting equation?
r: Assets and liabilities are both understated by $4,000
The equipment and the debt were left out.
w: Assets and equity are understated by $4,000
The purchase was on account, not by the owner.
Assets are understated, liabilities are overstated
There is no effect because the equation still balances
The equation balances but with wrong totals.

q: Which of the following sequences is correct?
r: Journalize, post, prepare the trial balance, adjust, prepare statements, close
This follows the standard accounting cycle.

q: What is a ledger account balance?
r: The difference between total debits and total credits in an account
It shows the net amount for the account.
w: The total of all entries ignoring side
Debits and credits are netted against each other.
The date of the last entry
A balance is a dollar amount.

q: What is a debit?
r: An entry on the left side of an account
It increases assets and expenses.
w: An entry on the right side of an account
A request for payment sent to a customer

q: What is a credit?
r: An entry on the right side of an account
It increases liabilities, equity and revenue.
w: An entry on the left side of an account
A discount offered to a buyer

q: The Cash account has debits of $12,000 and credits of $8,400. What is its balance?
r: $3,600 debit
Debits exceed credits by this amount.
w: This is only the credit total.

q: What is the purpose of a subsidiary ledger?
r: To hold detailed records supporting a control account
Accounts receivable can be broken down by customer.
w: It supplements the journal and ledger.
To record the owner's personal transactions
Personal items are not business records.

q: The Accounts Receivable control account shows $18,500, but the customer subsidiary ledger totals $18,050. What should the bookkeeper do?
r: Investigate for a posting or addition error
The two should always agree.
w: Ignore it because the difference is small
Adjust the control account to match without checking
Corrections must be based on finding the cause.

q: What is a journal entry's explanation (narration) for?
r: To describe the transaction in words
It helps others understand why the entry was made.
w: To hide the transaction from auditors
The trial balance uses account totals.

q: What is the effect on the accounting equation of paying $500 for rent?
r: Assets decrease by $500 and equity decreases by $500
Cash goes down and expenses reduce equity.

q: A business sells $750 of goods on account. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
r: Assets increase by $750 and equity increases by $750
Receivables and revenue both go up.
w: The sale is revenue, not debt.
Assets increase with the new receivable.

q: Which of these is a permanent account?
r: Accounts Payable
Permanent accounts carry balances into the next period.

q: After closing entries, what is the balance in the Rent Expense account?
r: Zero
Expense accounts are closed to start the next period fresh.
w: That is the balance before closing.
The amount of rent still owed
